item.title: Germany: Christmas markets open across the country amid tight security
item.description: Christmas markets across Germany are welcoming visitors with dazzling lights, traditional treats and festive attractions. Security remains a priority following deadly attacks in recent years.

item.title: Thanksgiving storms flood US coasts and disrupt holiday travel
item.description: Macy's has postponed its 100th parade in Manhattan as more than 600,000 homes and businesses lost power.

item.title: France's presidential hopefuls speak to Euronews as they court local politicians for endorsements
item.description: Although around forty figures have so far declared their intent to run in the presidential election — or are seen as potential candidates — not all will go the full way.

item.title: UK: London's Gingerbread City returns with 50 edible architectural creations
item.description: London architects have created a miniature city featuring gingerbread skyscrapers, sugar rivers and iconic landmarks. The festive exhibition also explores the future of urban living.

item.title: Belgium: Farmers and tractors descend on Brussels to defend EU subsidies
item.description: Around 200 representatives of European farming unions marched through Brussels, Belgium, on Thursday 26 November 2026 to protest against proposed cuts to the European Union's Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The demonstration coincided with a summit on the bloc's next long-term budget.

item.title: UK-EU food deal carries exit penalty, legal text shows
item.description: Political parties Reform UK and the Conservatives have both signalled they would consider unpicking Andy Burnham's Brexit reset if they win power at the next general election in 2029.

item.title: Son of Myanmar's Suu Kyi 'relieved' by first call in five years, questions military's motives
item.description: Speaking to Euronews’ The World Conversation, Kim Aris described his relief at hearing his mother’s voice after five years, called for tougher sanctions enforcement and defended her record on the Rohingya genocide ruling.

item.title: Euronews Verify: How can the EU continue to afford supporting Ukraine?
item.description: The European Commission last week unveiled a €45 billion loan to help Ukraine amid Russia's nonstop airstrikes. But how is the EU affording all this support?

item.title: NATO deploys AWACS airborne radar to monitor Polish airspace
item.description: NATO has authorised deploying an AWACS reconnaissance aircraft to Poland after prosecutors said three Russian cruise missiles fell on its territory. The flying radar has served since the Cold War, in the Balkans, in Libya and after 11 September over US airspace.

item.title: Argentina enters technical recession as weak consumption undermines Milei's economic gains
item.description: Argentina's economy shrank 1.8% in the third quarter, its second straight contraction. Weak consumption, falling purchasing power and strain in key sectors are slowing growth and clouding Javier Milei's prospects.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 26th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Europe Tonight: EU leaders clash over record-high budget amid Ukraine funding standoff
item.description: EU leaders are clashing at the European Council over a record-high long-term budget, divided on defense, farm subsidies, and Ukraine aid. Germany threatens a veto unless all sign on to Ukraine funding, while Spain’s Sánchez skips the summit ahead of Sunday’s election, delegating his vote to Macron.

item.title: Hong Kong mourns victims of deadly Wang Fuk Court fire one year on
item.description: Hong Kong residents lay flowers and pay tribute to the 168 victims of the Wang Fuk Court fire in China, one year after the deadly disaster.

item.title: Gérard Depardieu to stand trial over rape accusations by actress Charlotte Arnould
item.description: The 77-year-old actor is accused by actress Charlotte Arnould, then 22, of raping her twice in August 2018. The appeal court confirmed he will stand trial for one of the alleged rapes.

item.title: Anthropic chief denies wanting humans to 'surrender' free will to AI
item.description: Dario Amodei's comments come amid a growing debate over how to maintain human autonomy in the face of superintelligent AI systems.

item.title: Iraq sentences eight French nationals to life for joining Islamic State
item.description: Two other French citizens have been sentenced to 15 years in prison, while the verdict has been postponed for 10 additional French nationals by the court.

item.title: From volume to value: making tourism work for more of Europe
item.description: Tourism deserves a central place in European policymaking, writes Peter Lochbihler of Booking.com in an opinion piece for Euronews. The EU should support lesser-known destinations in attracting visitors worldwide, fostering local revitalisation, growth and prosperity.

item.title: Nordic countries: A European gateway to space? | Euronews Tech Talks
item.description: The Arctic has become strategically important for Europe. But can the region play a central role in helping the EU reach its ambitions in space?

item.title: French presidential candidate Raphaël Glucksmann to Euronews: 'France's vote will shape Europe's destiny'
item.description: France's future relationship with Europe has emerged as a central campaign issue ahead of elections in spring 2027, amid divisions over European integration, French sovereignty and support to Ukraine.

item.title: Jordan Bardella denies fresh wave of antisemitism allegations
item.description: Bardella, who is vying to become France's next prime minister on a joint ticket with Marine Le Pen, faced allegations in September that he made conspiracist comments about Jewish people on Facebook in 2013.

item.title: Aerial footage shows diesel tanker sinking off Ibiza
item.description: A tanker carrying around 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off Ibiza, prompting Spanish authorities to assess the risk of marine pollution. One crew member died after all 17 people on board were rescued.

item.title: Temu agrees to change commercial practices in EU, says Commission
item.description: The Chinese retailer had been found in breach of EU consumer rules for not doing enough to stop the sale of illegal and unsafe products on its website, which could have led to a fine of up to 6% of its global annual turnover. The company has now made commitments to follow EU consumer rules.

item.title: Eurozone leaders back Hernández de Cos to succeed Lagarde at ECB
item.description: Eurozone leaders meeting in Brussels backed Hernández de Cos to lead the European Central Bank, which sets interest rates for the 21 countries that use the euro.

item.title: What makes a city attractive? AI ranks Budapest’s centre among the world’s top 10
item.description: Budapest city centre ranked as the world's 10th most attractive downtown in an international AI study using street views to gauge liveability. The historic core is world class, but poor comfort and struggling suburbs mean the whole capital only came 42nd.

item.title: Russia launches ballistic missile and drone barrage on Ukraine, killing at least three
item.description: Ukraine's air defences downed 87 Russian missiles and drones overnight on Thursday. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drones struck a chemical plant making components for military explosives and a power station in the Stavropol region.

item.title: From electric flying taxis in Guangzhou to digital hangars in Beijing: how China is reshaping air travel
item.description: China is testing passenger flying taxis in Guangzhou and digitising aircraft maintenance in Beijing, as it pushes new technology into every stage of air travel.

item.title: ‘Is James Bond conservative?': Trump gives verdict on Robert Pattinson – but asked about 007's politics first
item.description: Donald Trump has given Robert Pattinson his blessing after the actor was announced as the next James Bond. First, however, Trump reportedly asked whether Bond was a conservative. You can't make this up...

item.title: Kyoto's iconic autumn foliage draws crowds of visitors
item.description: Tourists flock to Kyoto, Japan, to admire vibrant autumn foliage as red, orange and golden maple leaves transform the former imperial capital.

item.title: Passenger flights diverted as Kuwait army intercepts Iranian drone attack
item.description: Kuwait's military said four people were injured after "a number of hostile" Iranian drones were detected and intercepted in its airspace. Flights crossing Iraq toward the Gulf were given new headings ahead of Kuwait, shifting the international corridor.

item.title: Fathers' antidepressant use tied to slight blood pressure risk in kids — but drugs may not be why
item.description: Researchers said their findings should offer reassurance for hopeful fathers who take antidepressants.

item.title: Farmers demonstrate in Brussels against EU budget cuts
item.description: Francie Gorman, President of the Irish Farmers Association, warns that cuts to the common agricultural policy could threaten their livelihoods, food security and the future of European farming.

item.title: Judges in Netanyahu corruption trial urges dropping key charges
item.description: Israel continues to struggle to form a government after the 27 October election. Netanyahu has denied wrongdoing in all three cases since his trial began in May 2020.

item.title: Ashes to ashes: FC Barcelona reveals plans to let Camp Nou be fans' final resting place
item.description: Extra-time may soon have a different meaning for fans of FC Barcelona. Supporters are now being offered the chance to keep their ashes at the Spanish football club, under recently announced plans to build a memorial within the walls of the famous Camp Nou stadium.

item.title: Watch as rare cloud 'waterfall' cascades over Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The natural phenomenon went viral on social media, forcing photographers to confirm that it wasn't produced by artificial intelligence.

item.title: TUI boss wants EU to cut bureaucracy, attract talent and expand green energy
item.description: Euronews spoke with TUI's CEO Sebastian Ebel about manure-powered cruise ships, migration, dependence on the US, Artificial Intelligence, and the future of tourism.

item.title: Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic suspends flights as bankruptcy looms
item.description: Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic, hit by surging jet fuel prices due to the war against Iran, said on Thursday that it was teetering on the verge of bankruptcy as it cancelled all flights for the day.

item.title: Flames and thick smoke billow from Bangkok oil facility after massive explosion
item.description: A powerful explosion rocks an oil depot in Bangkok, Thailand, sending thick black smoke into the sky and prompting evacuation warnings.

item.title: Feminists march across Spain against violence ahead of general election
item.description: Demonstrations for the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women come just days before elections in which the far right could approach 20% of the vote.

item.title: ‘The taste layer of the internet ’: Reddit's COO on why AI needs humans
item.description: Euronews Next spoke to Jen Wong about the threat of AI to the open internet and the importance of human connection on the platform.

item.title: From Vice City to gaming suites: How Grand Theft Auto VI is changing the way people travel
item.description: From hotels with dedicated gaming rooms to real-life destinations featured in blockbuster titles, video games are increasingly influencing holiday plans. New data reveals a surge in searches for gaming-themed stays, with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI helping fuel the trend.

item.title: Images show Kim Jong Un inspecting North Korean nuclear facilities
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has called for expanding the country's nuclear arsenal after visiting nuclear material production facilities and a weapons research institute.

item.title: Why the Mediterranean is a hotspot for oil spills after tanker sinks near Ibiza
item.description: Any pollution entering the water could have a possible impact on Mediterranean seagrasses that absorb substantial quantities of climate-heating carbon dioxide.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 26th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Musk says will give two SpaceX shares to 'every child in America'
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said on Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month.

item.title: EU must find new revenue or scale back spending plans, MEP says
item.description: EU leaders are meeting in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s next seven-year budget.

item.title: US says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites to build data centres in space
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's rocket company to create a data centre constellation to power AI on earth.

item.title: After initial reluctance, Bulgaria says it's 'ready' to join €45 billion Ukraine loan
item.description: Bulgaria will contribute to the new €45 billion support loan to Ukraine, Prime Minister Rumen Radev confirmed on Thursday. But the country will not help pay for weapons and ammunition.

item.title: Less sex, more screens: Britain’s sexual habits are changing
item.description: One in three 16- to 24-year-olds have never had sex, up from one in five in 2010.

item.title: UK sent Sri Lankan refugee to Eswatini in secret deal, the BBC says
item.description: The United Kingdom reportedly sent a Sri Lankan refugee who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, where he committed suicide, as part of a secret deal, according to an investigation by the BBC.

item.title: Cheaper, generic HIV prevention drug arrives in Zambia
item.description: The rollout in Zambia is part of a plan to ensure people in lower-income countries can access the breakthrough HIV prevention drug.
